heterogeneidade.descricao: Narrativa versus tabela para parallel: a seção 3 afirma que parallel melhora a qualidade em relação a serial e any. Na Tabela 1, Avg Speedup K = 1: Parallel 1.36 e Serial 1.35 (7B), Parallel 1.50 e Serial 1.50 (14B); Direct, condição não descrita, tem 1.81 (7B) e 2.31 (14B), acima de Parallel. Diferenças maiores a favor de Parallel sobre Serial aparecem no Aggregated Best K = 100 (2.40 vs 1.96 no 7B; 2.09 vs 1.71 no 14B). Se Direct correspondesse a any, a narrativa contradiria a tabela; o estudo não estabelece essa correspondência.

Para multi-stage, a seção 3 diz que o speedup médio não mostra melhora significativa e que o máximo aumenta, sem nomear a condição de comparação nem relatar teste estatístico. Na Tabela 1 (7B, Avg K = 1), Multi-Stage tem 1.86, frente a 1.36 de Parallel, 1.35 de Serial e 1.81 de Direct; no 7B, Avg cai de 1.86 (K = 1) para 1.65 (K = 10).

A RAG padrão tem Avg Speedup K = 1 abaixo de Direct (1.66 vs 1.81 no 7B; 1.95 vs 2.31 no 14B) e acima de Parallel (1.66 vs 1.36; 1.95 vs 1.50). A seção 3 diz que a RAG padrão 'can negatively impact' a qualidade sem indicar a condição de referência.

Inversão entre tamanhos de modelo: em RAG+Self-Match, o 14B fica abaixo do 7B em Avg K = 100 (3.75 vs 3.81), Aggregated Best K = 10 (4.84 vs 5.46) e Aggregated Best K = 100 (5.13 vs 6.06), embora fique acima em Avg K = 1 (3.98 vs 3.29) e Avg K = 10 (3.94 vs 3.77). A média por K também varia com K no 14B (3.98, 3.94, 3.75), sem informação sobre variabilidade.

Os valores do resumo e da conclusão (6.06X e 5.13X) correspondem ao Aggregated Best Speedup com K = 100 da condição RAG+Self-Match, isto é, ao máximo de 100 gerações; o resumo não especifica a métrica nem o K. As médias correspondentes (Avg K = 100) são 3.81 e 3.75.

citacoes.trecho: Finally planning-oriented prompting, code verification and retrieval augmented editing are used to promote the actual performance of the LLM generated code.
The evaluation results confirm that a rough speedup of 6.06X and 5.13X are achieved using Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct, Qwen2.5-Coder-14B-Instruct LLM models.
Positive improvement is confirmed in our experiment with three LLM models (GPT-4o-mini, Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct, Qwen2.5-Coder-14B-Instruct).
Planning is pivotal to the prompting workflow, including both single-stage prompts for direct parallelization and decomposed workflows for multi-stage code transformation.
The four prompt types represent different planning granularities:
serial: Do not explicitly specify a parallelization method; instead, instruct the model to rewrite and optimize the serial source code.
any: Suggest OpenMP parallel optimization as an available option, requiring the model to rewrite the serial source code into faster code without restrictions on serial or parallel execution.
multi-stage: Decompose the optimization process into two stages: first, perform serial optimization, and then apply parallel to convert the code optimized in the first stage into parallel code.
For LLMs with larger parameter sizes or broader context windows, the error information is explicitly fed back to the model, prompting it to regenerate the code.

As the code generated by LLMs may potentially yield incorrect results, we implement a self-correction mechanism that enables the LLM to predict, verify, and rectify the functionality of the generated code.
Based on this analysis, the LLM then regenerates the code to ensure functional correctness and the correctness rate is further improved with this technique.

To address potential inconsistencies in function interfaces that may arise from large language models (LLMs), we employ the nm tool to analyze the abstract syntax tree (AST) of the compiled object files.

Initially, We discovered some outliers in the speedup records of the synthesized data and identified two reasons for this: (1) erroneous code that occasionally passed all the program-generated test cases; (2) the speedup of some code is highly dependent on the test data.
If all tests pass, we calculate the average speedup after removing extremums to mitigate noisy speedup signals.
All long entries with token counts exceeding 1,000 will be eliminated, and finally 5,841 of these long entries were removed from the PIE dataset.
We perform multiple inferences on 60 questions from the ParEval dataset [17], collecting 500 effective samples for each question, and in total 30,000 distinct target code examples are gathered.

When a new program is received for optimization, the system retrieves the L most similar programs from this knowledge base based on their embeddings, and for practical cases, L can be set to be 1,2,3.
With the introduction of retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), the prompt includes the two most similar {source code: target code} pairs to guide the model.
The default version of RAG can retrieve two samples with identical source code, which, as observed from the experimental results, can negatively impact the quality of the generated code.
Therefore, we incorporated self-match verification to ensure that the two retrieved samples have different source codes, significantly enhancing the code quality.
Your goal is to rewrite serial code to make it fast through parallel processing.
